hypotheses.title: Systematic Risk Decile Inversion Anomaly (Betting Against Beta)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Exploits the structural low-beta anomaly (Baker et al. 2011; Frazzini & Pedersen 2014). Institutional investors constrained by leverage limits over-allocate to high-beta stocks to achieve higher nominal returns, creating persistent overvaluation in high-beta names. Subindustry-neutralized negative 60-day rolling beta (-beta_last_60_days_spy) isolates defensive, high-quality equities that produce positive risk-adjusted returns while immunizing against market down-draws. Natural slow variation in rolling regression parameters ensures low turnover (~7-9%) to maximize Fitness.
confounders: Prolonged market melt-up rallies where speculative high-beta equities temporarily outpace defensive names
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if low-beta equities consistently underperform within subindustries during sideways or bear market regimes.

candidates.rationale: 5-day linear decay on backfilled 60-day market beta, cross-sectionally ranked within subindustry.

hypotheses.title: Supply Chain Customer Return Spillover Momentum
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Capitalizes on customer-supplier information diffusion friction (Cohen & Frazzini 2008). Return signals of major corporate customers (pv13_custretsig_retsig) predict the subsequent equity performance of their suppliers over intermediate horizons due to market inattention to cross-firm economic linkages. Smoothing with 5-day linear decay filters transient noise while capturing institutional supply-chain drift with ~6-8% turnover.
confounders: Customer-specific idiosyncratic shocks that do not translate into supplier order book changes
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if customer return signal exhibits zero forward predictive power on supplier returns over 15-day horizons.

candidates.rationale: 10-day backfilled customer return signal smoothed over 5 days with subindustry neutralization.

hypotheses.title: Balance Sheet Liquidity Buffer — Cash to Short-Term Debt Solvency
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Evaluates corporate solvency resilience via the cash-to-short-term-debt coverage ratio relative to its trailing 1-year historical baseline (ts_rank(..., 252)). Equities expanding liquid reserves against impending debt maturities are insulated from debt rollover crunches and liquidity shocks, outperforming leveraged peers. Unit-safe 0.0001*assets term prevents division by zero without dimension mismatch.
confounders: Cash hoarding driven by lack of productive capital expenditure opportunities
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if cash-rich companies underperform highly levered firms in tightening credit environments.

candidates.rationale: 1-year percentile rank of cash-to-short-term-debt ratio with asset-scaled division safeguard.
